steps.description: Verify the Authorization header contract: attempt to call a protected API endpoint (e.g. GET /api/v1/portals or equivalent list endpoint) without a Bearer token and confirm the server enforces authentication.

steps.expected: Server returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized. Response body contains an error or detail field. The endpoint does NOT return 200 or any data without a valid JWT.

steps.description: Verify the authenticated API surface: call the job portals list endpoint with the valid session JWT and confirm data is returned and scoped to the authenticated user.
steps.action: Use page.evaluate to send fetch('http://localhost:8001/api/v1/portals', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + <session_token_from_cookie_or_storage> } }), observe status and response body
steps.expected: HTTP 200 is returned. Response body is a JSON array or paginated object. All returned records belong to the authenticated user (no cross-user data leakage). An empty array [] is acceptable if no portals exist; a non-200 or non-JSON response is a failure.

steps.description: Exercise the CRUD create path: via the UI, create a new job portal entry (or equivalent resource) with a unique name to confirm the POST endpoint and UI wiring are functional.
steps.action: Navigate to the job portals list page (e.g. /jp/portals or /jp/dashboard), locate the 'Create' or 'Add Portal' button, click it, fill in required fields (name: 'JH-QA-Portal-' + Date.now(), and any other required fields), submit the form, wait for the list to refresh or a success state
steps.expected: New portal record appears in the list or a success confirmation is shown. No validation error blocks submission when all required fields are filled. HTTP 201 or 200 is returned from the backend. The record is visible in the list without a page refresh being required.

steps.description: Exercise validation on the create form: attempt to submit the portal creation form with required fields left blank to confirm the API and UI enforce field-level validation.
steps.action: Open the portal creation form again, leave the name/required fields empty, click the Submit button, observe UI feedback
steps.expected: Form does NOT submit to the backend (client-side validation blocks it), OR the backend returns HTTP 422 with a structured validation error. A visible error message is shown next to the empty required field(s). The user is not navigated away from the form.

steps.description: Exercise the rate-limit bucket introduced in v1.2: make 6 or more rapid successive requests to a protected endpoint and confirm the server enforces rate limiting without crashing.
steps.action: Use page.evaluate to fire 7 sequential fetch() calls to http://localhost:8001/api/v1/portals with the valid Bearer token in quick succession, collect all HTTP status codes
steps.expected: The first N requests (up to the bucket limit) return 200. Once the limit is exceeded, subsequent requests return HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. The server does not return 500 or drop the connection. Exact bucket size need not be asserted — presence of a 429 within 7 rapid calls is sufficient.

steps.description: Verify audit log persistence: after the CRUD create action in step 7, check whether the system surfaces an audit trail entry (via the UI audit tab or API) for the creation event.
steps.action: Navigate to the portal Audit tab or admin audit log section (if exposed in UI), or call GET /api/v1/audit-log (or equivalent) with the valid Bearer token, filter for the record created in step 7
steps.expected: At least one audit log entry references the portal created in step 7 (matched by name or ID). The entry includes a timestamp and action type (e.g. 'created'). If no audit UI exists, the endpoint returns 200 with an array — an empty array here is a defect to record, not a blocking failure.

steps.description: Verify cross-service integration: trigger a job scan on the portal created in step 7 and confirm the scan result or error is surfaced clearly — no silent failures.
steps.action: Navigate to the portal detail page for the portal created in step 7, locate the 'Trigger Scan' or 'Scan Now' button, click it, wait up to 10 seconds for a response
steps.expected: Either: (a) scan completes and job results appear in the scan history list, OR (b) a clear, user-visible error message explains why the scan could not proceed (e.g. missing API key). Silent failure (spinner that never resolves, blank page, no feedback after 10s) is a defect.

steps.description: Navigate away from the portal detail page to the dashboard, then return to the portal detail page to verify that portal data and scan history persist correctly across navigation.

steps.expected: Portal detail page loads and shows the same portal name, configuration, and scan history as before navigation. No data is lost, reset, or shown as loading indefinitely. HTTP 200 is returned on the portal detail fetch.

steps.description: Verify the Razorpay webhook endpoint is reachable and rejects unsigned/malformed payloads — confirming the security surface of the one unauthenticated POST route.

steps.expected: Server returns HTTP 400 or 401 (signature validation failure). It does NOT return 200 or process the payload. The endpoint is reachable (no 404, no 500 crash), confirming routing is correct while the security gate is enforced.

steps.description: Verify AES-256-GCM credential encryption invariant: confirm that any stored credential or API key value retrieved via the API is NOT returned in plaintext — it should be masked, omitted, or returned as a write-only sentinel.
